newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Serbian taxi drivers end strike.
newsitem.headline: Serbian taxi drivers end strike.

text.p: Protesting taxi drivers agreed to call off a strike in the Yugoslav capital on Wednesday, after late crisis talks between government and taxi union officials reached an agreement over vehicle taxes.
Earlier, police stopped several thousand taxi drivers from reaching government buildings in the city centre in their protest to demand tax cuts and an end to a ban on the import of second-hand cars.
Special police units in combat gear blocked the roads, but some protesters abandoned their cars and continued on foot amid traffic chaos.
The Serbian minister for private enterprise, Radoje Djukic, told a taxi drivers' rally that their demands were justified.
Milivoj Armus, head of Belgrade's biggest taxi company, said the protest had already been postponed for a month after the government promised to deal with their problems.
Senior government ministers agreed to meet taxi drivers' representatives, and later issued a statement outlining an agreement to reduce taxes.
A joint statement issued after thet meeting said the Serbian Public Revenue Bureau is to develop a new formula for calculating cab drivers' taxes by October 25, and issue revised tax assessments.
The statement also said the government would work with union officials to resolve outstanding complaints.
According to a spokesman for Belgrade's largest taxi company, Beotaxi, the outcome was "not bad", but he warned that drivers would adopt a "wait and see" attitude.
"If the government doesn't deliver (by October 25), we'll go out into the streets again and then we won't be held responsible for the consequences," he told Reuters.
Serbia has around 20,000 registered taxi drivers, of whom half are in Belgrade, which has a quarter of Yugoslavia's 11 million population.
High unemployment and low wages have pushed many people, including professionals, into cab driving.
The strike has added to tension in Serbia, which has recently been shaken by a wave of worker protests as the economy worsens.
